review.summary: Fix for wrong line numbers reported for syntax errors when lines end in semicolons. The issue (#494) clearly documents a regression from Julia 1.6 to 1.10 where error line numbers differ depending on trailing semicolons. The commit fixes parser.jl (production code) and includes test changes in test/expr.jl.
review.evidence: Issue #494 provides a clear MWE showing that lines ending in `;` cause incorrect line numbers in error messages (line 2 instead of line 4). PR #495 references 'Fix #494'. The commit modifies src/parser.jl (production code) and test/expr.jl (test code), consistent with a targeted bug fix for syntax trivia attachment to top-level statements.
review.missing_evidence: The actual diff content is not available, so I cannot verify the exact nature of the parser change or the specific test assertions added. The commit stats and file details are empty.
review.validation_risks: Without seeing the actual code change, there's a small risk that the fix involves broader refactoring of trivia handling that could affect other parse behaviors. The issue title of PR #495 ('Consistent attachment of syntax trivia to top level statements') suggests a somewhat broader scope than a single-line fix.
review.suggested_tests: 1. Parse `f(;1;2);\n` and verify the error points to the correct line. 2. Parse `f(;1;2)\n` without trailing semicolon and verify same line number. 3. Verify multi-line files with trailing semicolons report correct line numbers for subsequent errors. 4. Regression test ensuring trailing semicolons on non-error lines don't shift reported positions.
